- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent high, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, reduce the peak by 5–10% to account for over-optimism.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong upward trend, apply mean reversion bias: cap forecast at 10–15% below recent 5-day high.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.3) and forecast is erratic, smooth out extremes by averaging 3–5 prior values before forecasting.  
- When sentiment is near 0.5 and forecast is consistently below true outcome, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for underestimation.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3+ days, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day to correct for overconfidence bias.
